findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed food items such as but not limited to lettuce heads and other vegetables stored on the floor of the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC and vegetables were placed on shelves. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches from the floor or in a manner that protects against contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: During the inspection, an employee was observed to wash their hands and shut off the faucet without using a barrier. This heavier was corrected on site and the employee rewashed their hands with correct procedure. PIC will retrain staff on hand washing. Ensure staff wash their hands following correct hand washing procedures. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: 
-The gaskets of the refrigerators and freezers in the kitchen are observed to have an accumulation of dust/food debris. Ensure the current accumulation of dust/food debris is cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation and then ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
-The white shelving above the triple sink is observed to have an accumulation of dust and is in need of being cleaned. Ensure that the shelving is cleaned of the current accumulation and then is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop is observed to be stored with the mop head directly on the floor and unable to air dry. This mop was inverted and placed in a position able to air dry during the inspection. Ensure the mop is stored in a manner that allows it to air dry between uses.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

Ensure these surfaces are cleaned to remove the current buildup of accumulation and then ensure these surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The top of the white freezer next to the microwave is observed to have an excessive accumulation of dust/soil debris. On this surface is stored single service to-go containers. The bottom container is being discarded during today’s inspection and the sing service items are being moved from this location and will not be stored on this surface until it is cleaned and sanitized. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:

The bowls are not in contact with the paper on the food contact surface and so the facility has been advised to remove the contact paper and either change it out with new paper that is changed at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean or to remove the contact paper and replace it with a plastic or metal sheeting that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler was recorded at 58 degrees F at the start of the inspection. The cooler was observed in operating order during the hours of prep before the facility opened today which was less than 4 hours ago. The food items requiring cold holding below 41 degrees F and the eggs which require under 45 degrees F were moved into the white fridge along the cook line that was holding temperature. No food items remain in the cooler that are potentially hazardous at this time. Observation of the cooler will be made towards the end of the inspection to observe the temperature again. If records show the cooler above 41 degrees F, main entrance is required on the cooler. Facility has stated they will monitor the temperature again in the morning and call for service at that time if necessary.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by sponge and steel wool. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed a sponge and steel wool to be inside hand sink at facility prior to inspector washing hands. Maintain all hand sinks free of items in order to be accessible at all times. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13  (C) Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

Observed frozen fish to be thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) within walk-in cooler. Discussed thawing fish outside of ROP in order to hinder foodborne illness.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at front drink area. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

Observed multiple plastic cups to have condensation within and stacked properly at front drink area. Allow cups to adequately air-dry after cleaning and sanitizing before stacking. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple freezers throughout facility and walk-in cooler fan. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed multiple facility freezers to have food and/or soil debris within. Observed walk-in cooler fan to have a large accumulation of dust. Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC.

Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable. findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Front door has small gap in the bottom corner and along the side of the door that may allow for pest entry, and there are mouse droppings observed in several areas of the facility (bottom shelves in the kitchen with a significant amount, one on the rice container near the back door, and a few on a top shelf in the dry storage). PIC states that Orkin was just here this morning, but they no longer leave an invoice at the time of service. PIC states Orkin gives them glue traps to put down, but there is only one glue trap observed set up. Seal door to prevent pest entry and consult Orkin to eliminate pests. 

6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Facility has the Purrell Food Contact Surface spray bottles that they use on prep surfaces, but do not have the appropriate test strips for this product. Contact the company on the label to purchase test strips for this product.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: There are mouse droppings observed on the bottom shelves in the kitchen, one on the rice container near the back door and a few on the top shelf in the dry storage area. Clean these shelves.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Dish machine sanitizer dispenser unit is not operating. Machine does have a hot water booster, but the disc thermometer run through the machine two times only reached a maximum of 156F. Facility thought that something was wrong with the electrical portion of it and had it worked on, but the dispenser needs parts that will have to be ordered. In the meantime, PIC states that they are sanitizing in the 3 compartment sink. This sink will need to be set up to sanitize all dishware after being run through the dish machine for the wash and rinse portion of the wash, rinse, sanitize process. A spot check will be conducted once dish machine has been repaired to ensure that it is operating properly. 4-501.114  (P) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: Observed a hat and other personal items stored on a food prep surface. Do not store personal items where they have the potential to contaminate food and food prep areas. Store personal items in designated areas away from food and food prep areas. 6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: Facility has 4 food handler certificates available and 2 of them are for 2 of their Certified Food Protection Managers. All food handlers who do not have the Certified Food Protection Manager Certificate will need to complete the online ANSI approved food handler training course and have a certificate available. Make sure to check expiration dates for those certificates that are available as several expire in August of this year. 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed house made sauces in the walk in cooler that had date marking labels of 12/18, 12/19 and 12/20 on them. These were all reported to have been made on Monday, however, and the benefit of the doubt was given to the facility to re-date these items. Several old date marking labels were observed on other containers as well (with labels not matching what was inside). Make sure to accurately date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods including house made sauces and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed sauces in the reach in freezer that had been cooling with no indication as to when the cooling process began. Green sauce was probed at 101F, red sauce at 94F and the sauce in smaller containers 70F. Sauces were reported to have been made around noon, portioned and placed directly in the cooler around 2 pm. Sauces most likely remained at hot holding temperature for some time while in the freezer. Sauces were pulled and placed on an ice bath to rapidly cool them. Make sure when cooling, the time the cooling process begins is indicated and foods reach 70F within 2 hours and 41F or below within an additional 4 hours.
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
Old date marking labels are not being fully removed or removed at all in between use. Remove old date marking labels before washing, rinsing and sanitizing to avoid confusion.
750-830f Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor in the walk in cooler to be soiled black underneath the shelving units. Clean the floor.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.comment: See 9/18/2018 inspection report for details.

findings.comment: See 9/18/2018 inspection report for details.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: See 9/18/2018 inspection report for details.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed raw chicken in the reach in cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 56F. Beef in this same cooler was probed at 34F, however, the beef appeared to be thawing from frozen. Thermometer in this same cooler was reading 54F. Staff states they do not keep any foods in this cooler overnight and that the are in and out of it frequently. 2) Sauce in the other reach in cooler was probed at approximately 56F as well. There are multiple batches of chicken cooling in this cooler. Coolers must stay cool enough even during periods of service to keep foods at 41F or below. Chicken is reported that it will all be used this evening.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
1) Observed cooked chicken in the reach in cooler with no indication as to when the cooling process began. 2)REPEAT> Observed four containers of house made sauces that were made around noon and were cooling at room temperature outside of the walk in cooler. Cooling is an active process and must be done rapidly. The time the cooling process begins must be recorded and foods must be rapidly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and then to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours. Sauce was moved to the walk in cooler.
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee scratch head and proceed to put gloves on and handle food. Gloves were also worn when getting in and out of the walk in cooler (which contaminated gloves). Hands must be washed before putting on gloves, anytime hands may become contaminated, etc.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the shelf on the pass through window from the walk in cooler to the kitchen to be soiled with mold accumulation. Replace shelf if mold is not able to be cleaned off. Make sure materials are smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
No sanitizer buckets were prepared at the time of the inspection, and staff was not knowledgeable in how to prepare sanitizer. All staff should be knowledgeable in how to prepare sanitizer buckets and when to use. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Disposal sink to the right of the dish machine is not connected to the plumbing. They use a wet/dry vac to vacuum out the water from this sink and then dump the canister in the three compartment sink (see notes in General Comments on Page 2 regarding three compartment sink being used as a mop sink). Plumbing should be installed to drain this sink effectively.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings all along the wall to the left of the reach in cooler on the cook line side of the kitchen. Droppings are observed on the electrical box on this all and stuck all along the wall the length of the electrical wires that run along the wall. Orkin comes monthly. Consult Orkin for pest control, clean the wall and monitor for pest activity. /
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed a couple of tiles leading into the walk in cooler to be missing and bare wood observed at the threshold leading into the walk in cooler. Replace tiles and seal wood so that it is nonabsorbent.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed three containers of sauce that were made around noon to be cooling at room temperature outside of the walk in cooler. Cooling is an active process and must be actively monitored. The time the cooling process begins must be recorded and the food must reach 70F within 2 hours, once it has reached 70F within 2 hours, you have an additional 4 hours to cool the food to 41F or below for a total cooling time of 6 hours. Sauce was moved to the walk in cooler to correct the violation.
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
Observed an employee chopping cilantro and handling cilantro with bare hands. This is reported to be a garnish and not necessarily cooked. Avoid bare hand contact with ready to eat foods.
750-280 Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed dry rice stored in a galvanized steel garbage bin. Store rice in food grade containers that are smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to be testing at 0-10 ppm chlorine. Dish machine was primed and still did not test appropriately. Do not use dish machine until it has been serviced to test at 50 ppm chlorine. In the meantime, the three compartment sink will be set up for washing, rinsing and sanitizing of dishware.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the clean dish drain board of the dish machine to be soiled with a few mouse droppings. Orkin treated on 5/23/18. Drain board was cleaned during the inspection.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the fan in the walk in cooler with an accumulation of dust, 2) the shelf in the walk in cooler at the pass through door with friable mold, 3) the top of the dish machine with mouse droppings (Orkin treated as above-see General Comments), 4) the doors and outside of the dish machine with lime scale accumulation. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed personal items such as keys being stored on the deli slicer. Store employee belongings in designated areas away from food and food prep areas.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Facility does not have chlorine test strips to check the dish machine and sanitizer buckets. Provide test strips.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Dish machine was ran and tested at 0ppm Cl. The three compartment sink will be used to wash, rinse, and sanitize dishes. Contact GFS.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No employee with their FSSMC was present during the inspection. Inspector will follow up in 90 days.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed bulk powders with no labels underneath the prep area. Label containers with their proper name.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed two small bowls of chicken cooling in the reach in cooler with no time stamp of start time of cooling. Chicken was 91F via infrared thermometer. PIC stated it had start cooling 20 minutes prior.  A time was provided on the dry erase board to CORRECT the violation.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No employee with their FSSMC was present during start time of inspection. An employee with their FSSMC arrived during the inspection to CORRECT the violation.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Sanitizing temperature
findings.comment:
Dish machine was ran and had a maximum temperature of 112F at the final rinse temperature. The wash temperate was 154F. PIC stated Hobart had serviced the machine a couple weeks prior. PIC was going to contact Hobart to service the machine. Dishes will be wash, rinsed, and sanitized in the three compartment sink to CORRECT the violation.
750-830 All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dish washing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility only has one employee with their FSSMC. This is considered insufficient. Facility should have at least two employees with their food managers certificate.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed no time stamp on the chicken in the reach in cooler for the start time of the cooling process. Chicken was 89F with infrared thermometer. PIC stated the chicken had been cooling for 30 minutes. Items should be time stamped with start time of cooling to insure food gets down to 70F within two hours and 41F with an additional four hours.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1)Observed dust accumulation on the corner of the wall near where the produce is stored for cooking. Clean wall. 2) Both men's and women's restroom sinks were separated from the wall. Seal sinks to the walls.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Walk in cooler was holding temperatures from 32F to 44F with probe thermometer. Potentially hazardous food was moved to reach in coolers. PHF should not be stored in walk in cooler until it can hold proper cold holding temperatures of 41F or below. Facility had WIC serviced. Documentation states the walk in cooler needs a new evaporator. Repair cooler.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Walk in cooler was not holding proper cold holding temperatures. The following food items were discarded: Salmon-47F, probe, container of crab meat-48F, probe, large bowl of rice-56F, infrared. Service cooler. Do not store potentially hazardous food items in cooler until cooler holds 41F or lower. 2)Observed garlic and oil mixture(80F-probe) and cut tomatoes(68F) sitting on counter. Items were taken out of cold holding at 3:30 and will be discarded by 7:30pm to CORRECT the violation.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed 6-10 small bowls of chicken that had just been taken off the stove and wrapped at 95F. Chicken was immediately put in cooler to continue the cooling process and time stamped with start time of cooling. Chicken should reach 70F within two hours and 41F with an additional four hours. If chicken does not reach either one of these temperatures with the given amount of time chicken should be discarded or reheated to 165F and begin the cooling process again. 
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed rice sitting on kitchen counter upon arrival of inspection at 75F with infrared thermometer. Puma stated the rice had been sitting out since 11am. Rice was immediately discarded to CORRECT the violation.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed pepper sauce not labeled in the refrigerator.  If item is out of original container or prepared on site it must require a label. The sauce was labeled during the inspection.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor underneath the dish machine to be soiled.  Clean the floor.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a mop stored improperly.  The mop was inverted during the inspection.
750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in cooler door to not be tight fitting. Cold air can be felt escaping refrigeration unit. Foam insulation/stripping has been placed around door to eliminate gaps, however some gaps still remain. Filling in these gaps will help the unit hold temperature better and should cut down on how much the unit is running. Repair door to make sure door is tight fitting.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) The pipes and under side of the shelf above the cooking equipment is soiled with an accumulation of grease and food debris. 2) general surfaces of the wok stands are soiled with an accumulation of grease and char. Surfaces may be stained but remove any loose or sticky material that is accumulating on the surfaces of wok stand. 750-800 Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:

750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Squirt bottles of food were unlabeled as to their contents.  Label the bottles or the place where they are set to identify each bottle's contents.

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Opened ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food (pineapple) in a refrigerator was undated as to when the can was opened.  The food was moved to a commercial container and the container dated to CORRECT the violation.  The can had not been opened more than 7 days.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Four containers of pork were thawing at room temperature.  They were put in the walk-in cooler to continue thawing in the proper manner to CORRECT the violation.

750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
An opened can of pineapple and an opened can of pineapple were uncovered in refrigeration units.  The food in each can was moved to food grade containers and covered to CORRECT the violation.    (NOTE: Once opened, do not store acidic food like ketchup in the can.  Move it to a food grade container.)

750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Paint all unsealed boards with a light colored glossy paint so they are non-absorbent and easily cleanable.
